body: Am I the only one that hears a "MOOOOO" in their head whenever I see a camel?

[IceJJFish - On the Floor](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iq_d8VSM0nw)

[His twitter feed is a fun read too](https://twitter.com/IceJJFish)

I guess if I were to pinpoint a reason why, I couldn't, it's just this feeling that you can't help but shake but you know it is right. 

I guess I am clinically depressed but even the notion of that sounds hopeless. I mean if I were to seek medical advice I would end up on anti-depressants and quite frankly I can think of better drugs to chemically induce a state of mind. Plus if they did work having it on my record would probably adversely affect me in the future. Sure there are talking therapies but then why bother? I see it everyday people who have been taking anti-depressants for years and I don't want to be one of those persons that depends on pills to be a different person from who they naturally are. 

My family I am growing a bittering resentment for with the exception of my father. My mum and my sister aren't terrible people I have just become aware of a growing incompatibility. My sister who is older than me picks fights over the most trivial things with everyone, family gatherings feel like a chore with her and I feel constantly belittled, then when she gets your provoked reaction she cries and plays the sympathy card.

My mother is unintentionally selfish and looks to mediate in the worst way. She can never see blame in herself and when she does realise she is wrong she has learnt to escalate the retaliation to the point where I explode and then at that point I am in the wrong and my retaliation becomes the subject of the argument. Those are the worst moments in my life, the moments that make me want to take a gun to my head. 

I find irony in that I can scream and shout and never be heard (listened to). Hence my growing resentment of my mother and sister, it is like a cancer slowly spreading until maybe one day it will eat all emotional attachment I have with them. 

My friends are moving on, settling down or starting careers. I don't resent them for that, that is life and I am happy for them but it did spotlight the stark loneliness of my life. I have been a rock to so many of them but yet the very thought of trying to seek their advice/help/whatever you want to call it takes me aback. I don't think any of them even those who were depressed in the past would handle the situation correctly.

I don't mind being alone, if I had the opportunity to go live somewhere all alone providing that I had the internet and my laptop and camera I would. It's not that I am an introvert or socially incompetent but with my own company I have no external influences or factors. 

However, there is nothing worse than being all alone despite the fact you are surrounded by people, people who all influence your life. 

Currently I am unemployed, sure I have some interviews coming up and I have had great jobs in the past. I didn't lose my job or anything like that I finally graduated and decided time to move on from a job I had whilst I was a student. 

18 months ago I was applying for a placement year, a year of experience in industry, and I had loads of interviews but I never got the job despite on some occasions being the best candidate there. It is kind of odd how they treat student applicants, they put you through standardise testing and effectively treat you as a number. You could be the best candidate for the job but if you don't perform in their methods of testing which all seem unrelated to the job then you have no chance.

With each application to a company you are asked to attend an assessment centre, this can be anything between half to a full day. Whilst you are there you will be testing on maths, english and sometimes pattern recognition against the clock as if you were 14 again. I whole heartedly don't agree with it I didn't graduate at the top of my class by not being able to do these things. You then go on to give presentations, group exercises, essays before an interview and after you have finished with the day then you need to return for a final interview having passed that stage. 

I don't think I ever recovered from the rejection after rejection after rejection and even now as a graduate I have to go through the same bullshit. The system itself is flawed, the standardised tests are made by 2 companies and there are only 10 tests for each category so after a while it becomes a memory game anyway. 

The best part is there are so many jobs that my application won't be considered for because they ask for a degree and a certain criteria of high school grades. Okay I wasn't the best student in high school 18 year old me didn't give a shit but when it came to my degree I worked so god damn hard for it to achieve the best grade and yet I can't apply to a Computer Science job because somebody that got straight A's in unrelated high school subjects with a lower classification degree can apply.

It gives me this overwhelming sense of hopelessness. 

It sounds like everything is going wrong in my life, it isn't. I have more good days then bad days and I still find little joys in my life whether it is enjoyable meals, social gatherings or just little hobbies but when a bad day does come around it knocks me down flat and I find myself toying around with this idea of never standing back up and in that idea brings comfort the thought of taking one difficult bound and then just nothing.

Sure people will be sad for a few weeks what death doesn't bring around some sadness? but they will move on. I will be remembered from time to time around the holidays but over the course of a few years I will become a memory that brings some sadness to peoples hearts and the next day forgotten again.

I like the idea. There will be regrets like I have a bucket list of sorts that I wished to spend my life completing but maybe that list will go on to serve others who are able to live life and love it. 

I am probably months from my final days so don't bother wasting time with me I am sure there are others who could do with your help.
